summary: This bill requires the Office of Management and Budget to consider creating a separate Standard Occupational Classification code for direct support professionals during its next system revision and to report to Congress if it chooses not to.

scores.thoughts: The bill explicitly states in section 5 that 'No additional funds are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this Act.' It is a narrow administrative directive to OMB regarding occupational classification and does not authorize, expand, or reduce any government spending programs.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection of any kind.

While the bill references establishing a classification code 'as a healthcare support occupation,' it does not address healthcare coverage, delivery models, public vs. private systems, or any policy on the healthcare market. The focus is solely on statistical classification for labor data.
No provisions or references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions related to immigration policy, visas, border security, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions related to reproductive rights, abortion access, or restrictions.
No provisions related to military, defense spending, or national security appropriations.
No provisions related to environmental regulations, climate policy, or natural resource management.

The bill discusses support for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities but only in the context of labor-market data collection for direct support professionals. It does not expand, contract, or alter any welfare, Medicaid, or safety-net program eligibility or funding.
No provisions related to schools, education funding, school choice, or federal education policy.
No provisions related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance abuse policy.
No provisions related to sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions related to trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill contains an explicit 'no new funds' clause and does not authorize any spending or borrowing, but it also does not enact any debt-reduction measures.
No provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No provisions related to foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions related to voting access, election integrity, or electoral processes.
No provisions related to technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill aims to improve labor-market data collection for a specific occupation but does not address union rights, collective bargaining, worker protections, or employer flexibility.
No provisions related to religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination law.
